Run sc-ExWAS across multiple exposures

Source: R/multi-exwas.R
run_multi_exwas.Rd

Convenience wrapper that runs run_sc_exwas for each exposure and combines results with a final global FDR correction across all exposures and cell types.

Usage

run_multi_exwas(
  x,
  exposures = NULL,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  covariates = NULL,
  min_cells = 10L,
  min_donors = 5L,
  filter_genes = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

exposures

Character vector. Exposure names to test. Default: all exposures in exposureData except the covariates.

celltype_col

Character. colData column with cell type labels. Default "cell_type".

covariates

Character vector (optional). Columns of exposureData adjusted for in every model; they are not tested as exposures, and listing one in exposures is an error.

min_cells

Integer. Default 10.

min_donors

Integer. Default 5.

filter_genes

Logical. Default TRUE.

...

Further arguments of run_sc_exwas, such as method or celltypes. An argument that run_sc_exwas does not accept is an error.

Value

A DataFrame with all results combined and padj_all for global FDR across all tests. The se and statistic fields retain the selected backend's semantics: edgeR QL has numeric-NA coefficient standard errors and a signed square-root QL F statistic, whereas DESeq2 and voom-dream return their coefficient standard errors with Wald and moderated t statistics, respectively. The columns are those of run_sc_exwas followed by padj_all; metadata(result)$per_exposure keeps the metadata() (parameters and diagnostics) of each exposure's run_sc_exwas result.

Details

If run_sc_exwas stops for one of the exposures, the call stops too, with an error that names the exposure, instead of leaving that exposure out of padj_all. A cell type that run_sc_exwas skips for an exposure with a warning, for example for too few donors with complete data, adds no tests to padj_all; the diagnostics in metadata(result)$per_exposure list the cell types fitted for each exposure.

Examples

library(SingleCellExperiment); library(S4Vectors)
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(5000, 8), nrow = 50,
    dimnames = list(paste0("G", 1:50), paste0("c", 1:100)))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(cell_id = paste0("c", 1:100),
        donor_id = rep(paste0("D", 1:5), each = 20),
        cell_type = rep(c("Mono", "NK"), 50)))
exp_mat <- matrix(rnorm(15), nrow = 5,
    dimnames = list(paste0("D", 1:5), c("E1", "E2", "E3")))
scee <- build_scee(sce, exp_mat, sample_col = "donor_id")
multi <- run_multi_exwas(scee,
    exposures = c("E1", "E2"),
    celltype_col = "cell_type",
    min_cells = 5L, min_donors = 3L)
#> Running sc-ExWAS for: E1
#> Running sc-ExWAS for: E2
